subject: Re: Redwood trial - procurement & billing next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Cc: Priya Shah <pshah@omnihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 17:12:00 -0800
Subject: Redwood trial — procurement & billing next steps (post-call recap)

Tom — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps:

Summary:
- Trial scope: 30-day trial for the clinical summarization workflow (up to 1M tokens/month).
- Success criteria: 80% of sampled summaries meeting QA rubric (see attached worksheet) and <250ms 95th percentile latency for API calls.

Procurement path:
- OmniHealth prefers a PO-based purchase for production; during the trial they can use a company card for any incidental charges but plan to move to PO for paid start.
- Expected procurement timeline: internal approvals by end of Feb; PO submission in first week of March (subject to legal review).

Commercial items to confirm:
- Billing start: agree to start billing at the earlier of (a) trial conversion date or (b) when usage exceeds the 1M token threshold.
- Contracting: you indicated interest in using the Azure marketplace for procurement; we can provide a marketplace invoice if you prefer.

Next steps:
1) I’ll send the SOW + worksheet (attached) for your procurement team.
2) Can you confirm whether the PO is for Redwood Hosted (SaaS) or Dedicated capacity? That affects billing terms.
3) Looping Dev (legal) and Ava (CS) for setup and success criteria questions.

If that all looks right, I’ll schedule a short kickoff with your procurement and engineering teams for the week of Feb 22.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OmniHealth_SOW_draft.pdf; procurement_worksheet.xlsx

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Couple quick clarifications:

- Procurement: confirmed — we'll aim to submit a PO for the paid contract. For the trial period, we can put a temporary card on file for any overages, but main intent is PO.
- Marketplace: Procurement prefers using Azure marketplace if you can support the same pricing/term structure there. Can you confirm if Marketplace billing will match Redwood's hosted pricing and whether we can sign a marketplace order form?
- Billing start: We prefer billing to start when we formally convert (i.e., when PO is issued and countersigned). However, if we cross the usage threshold earlier, would Redwood allow a 14-day grace to avoid unexpected charges while procurement completes?

I'll aim to get internal approvals this week. Looping Priya (procurement) here.

Thanks,
Tom

Thanks Tom — good questions. Answers below and looping in our legal/CS leads to confirm Marketplace and grace period details.

- Marketplace: Logan (cc'ed via separate thread) confirmed that Azure Marketplace can be supported. Marketplace orders generally mirror hosted pricing, but there’s an extra marketplace fee line item; I’ve asked Dev to confirm any contractual changes required for a marketplace order.

- Billing start / grace: We can offer a 14-day grace window if usage exceeds the trial threshold while you await the PO. Billing would normally begin on PO effective date, but if you exceed the trial limits we’ll notify you and hold charges for up to 14 days to avoid surprises — after that standard billing applies.

- Hosted vs Dedicated: Please confirm which capacity you plan to consume for production. If Dedicated is preferred, we’ll need to capture expected peak throughput to size the GPU pool; that will affect lead times.

Next actions for us:
- Dev: please confirm marketplace contract implications and whether a DocuSign/SOW flow is required.
- Ava: can you own onboarding checklist and the kickoff with OmniHealth's engineers? Target week of Feb 22.

Tom/Priya — can you confirm procurement's target date for PO submission (week of Mar 1?) and whether the PO will reference Redwood's Hosted SKU or Dedicated SKU?

Thanks,
Marissa

--

Enterprise Account Executive

Tom/Priya — quick note from legal/procurement side:

- Marketplace: We support Azure Marketplace billing and can route invoicing through the marketplace. Pricing parity will be preserved for the trial period; marketplace-managed billing will add standard marketplace fees which OmniHealth will see on their invoice. We can provide a marketplace order form or a standard SOW + PO path — whichever you prefer.

- DocuSign/SOW: Attached is a lightweight SOW template we usually use for trials. If you want DocuSign countersignature, we can prepare that. (Attachment: OmniHealth_SOW_draft.pdf)

- PO language: Please ensure the PO references Redwood Inference, Inc. and includes the SKU codes: RWI-HOST-TRIAL and RWI-HOST-STD (or RWI-DED-STD if you choose Dedicated). If procurement needs an internal contact for billing, use billing@redwood.ai.

- Billing start: Legal confirms billing starts on the PO effective date or marketplace order activation. We’re ok with the 14-day buffer developers requested; we’ll log overage notifications and hold charge capture until the buffer expires.

Happy to hop on a quick call if you want to run through the SOW.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
